flawed_step: Line 62 incorrectly claims that f <= 4 leaves only p = 5.
counterexample: Take p = 7. Then p is prime, p > 3, and f = (p-1)/2 = 3 <= 4. Thus the quoted bound does not exclude p = 7 (equivalently y = 14), contrary to line 62.
assessment_summary: The deduction omits the admissible case p = 7. The bound f <= 4 allows f = 2 (p = 5) and f = 3 (p = 7); only f = 4 gives the composite p = 9. Therefore the asserted reduction to only p = 5 is invalid.
